reasons: Frontmatter homes lists page '[[Collective Knowledge and the Fellow-Officer Rule]]' role 'Key', matching the payload.

Opinion's central question is 'whether the patrolman's stop and search ... was justified under the "collective knowledge" doctrine' and resolves it via vertical imputation (Zamudio-Carrillo) — squarely a Key case for that page.

Opinion two-step holding: 'asking first whether the DEA task force agents had probable cause ... They did. Second, we query whether the DEA task force's probable cause could be imputed to Patrolman Chavez. It could, in light of Zamudio-Carrillo' — supports imputation to the directed stopping officer.

Opinion: 'Patrolman Chavez, acting on the strength of the DEA task force's information, was objectively justified in initiating the stop and in searching the truck' and 'we affirm' — supports 'stop and search justified' and 'suppression properly denied'; TFO gave the patrolman only 'plate number, the vehicle description, the number of occupants' plus 'coke', confirming he was not privy to investigation details.
